title: Vehicle Signal Set
description: OBDb-v3-compatible per-vehicle signal definitions. Declares UDS/J1979 requests to a vehicle ECU and how to decode the byte response into physical signals. Adopted from the OBDb project (CC BY-SA 4.0) so existing community sets can be imported.

provenance.description: Where these definitions came from and how much to trust them.

canFormat.description: ISO-TP addressing width. 11bit for most BMW; 29bit required for GM Ultium (Lyriq).

commands.description: Each command is one request whose response yields one or more signals.

hdr.description: Request CAN id / tester address, hex. Sent to the adapter via 'AT SH'. E.g. '6F1' (BMW tester).

rax.description: Expected response CAN id, hex. Sent via 'AT CRA' to filter. E.g. '607' (BMW SME).

eax.description: Optional extended (target) address byte for BMW multi-ECU tester addressing, hex. E.g. '07' for the SME.

cmd.description: Single-entry map of {service: payloadHex}. '22' = UDS ReadDataByIdentifier (payload is the 2-byte DID). '01' = J1979 mode 01 (payload is the 1-byte PID). '19' = UDS ReadDTCInformation.

id.description: Stable signal id, unique within the set.

fmt.description: Bit-field extraction + linear scaling. Physical = (raw * mul / div) + add. IMPORTANT: 'bix' is the bit offset into the DATA PAYLOAD, i.e. the response bytes AFTER the service echo and the echoed 2-byte DID (for service 0x22) or 1-byte PID (for service 0x01) have been stripped. Big-endian.

bix.description: Start bit offset into the payload (big-endian). Defaults to 0.

sign.description: Interpret the raw field as two's-complement signed.
